podcast.title: Econoline Crush Formation and Early Juno Recognition (1992)
podcast.body: Formed in 1992, Econoline Crush received a Juno nomination within their first year of existence. "Within a year of forming in 1992 they nailed down a Juno nomination."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Initial Breakup (Post-2001)
podcast.body: Following the release of their third album, *Brand New History*, in 2001, Econoline Crush disbanded. "after a third album entitled Brand New History in 2001 they just called it quits."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Econoline Crush Reunion (2008)
podcast.body: Econoline Crush reunited in 2008, and this reunion appears to still be active. "before an Econoline Crush reunion to cold in 2008 which appears to still be an effect."

podcast.title: Collaboration with Bob Rock
podcast.body: "The Conorline Crush" is listed among Bob Rock's clients. "We got the cult, Veruch assault, Erasmith, Motley crew, Ardady Pease, the Tea Party, Eric and High Fy, Afghan Wigs, David Lee Roth, the Conorline Crush, Cher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Econoline Crush - Vancouver Alt Rock Prominence
podcast.body: Hailing from Vancouver, Econoline Crush was arguably the biggest alternative rock band from that city in the 1990s, second only to 5440. "the biggest alt rock band in the 90s to come out of Vancouver was Econoline Crush."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Econoline Crush Media Appearances
podcast.body: Econoline Crush's music was featured in various media, including TV shows like *Melrose Place*, ESPN sports coverage, and PlayStation games. "Econoline showed up in TV shows like Melrose Place and an ESPN sports coverage as well as in some PlayStation games."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Extensive Touring (Mid-1990s)
podcast.body: Within four years of their formation, Econoline Crush had released several successful albums and embarked on extensive tours with major acts such as Kiss, Foo Fighters, and Green Day. "Within four years they had a couple big albums and were touring with everyone from kiss to the food fighters to Green Day."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Frontman's Nursing Career
podcast.body: The band's sporadic activity led frontman Trevor Hurst to pursue a career in psychiatric nursing, working in an indigenous community and becoming an instructor. However, he had to quit nursing when the band seriously reactivated. "When a car line crush was seriously reactivated and started getting back to work, Trevor had to quit his nurse gig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Trevor Hurst – The Only Constant Member
podcast.body: Trevor Hurst has been the sole constant member of Econoline Crush, with almost three dozen other musicians having been part of the band at various times. "Singer Trevor Hurst has been the only constant member of Econoline Crush. There are almost three dozen former members."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Trevor Hurst's Band Hurst
podcast.body: Following Econoline Crush's initial breakup, singer Trevor Hurst formed his own band called Hurst. "Singer Trevor Hurst then formed his own band called Hurst."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Trevor Hurst's Nursing Career and Personal Journey
podcast.body: Trevor Hurst embarked on a new career as a nurse, earning his nursing degree from Brand New University at the age of 45. He has worked in Manitoba First Nations Reserves, assisting with addiction, after overcoming his own issues with alcohol by attending AA. "Trevor has a new gig as a nurse. He spent time in places like Manitoba First Nations Reserves helping people deal with addiction."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Vancouver Origins and Career Arc
podcast.body: Econoline Crush emerged from Vancouver in the early 1990s, led by frontman Trevor Hurst. They had a solid 10-year run before initially breaking up in 2002, but later returned in 2006 to record and perform sporadically, eventually reactivating more seriously. "Econoline Crush came out of Vancouver in the early 1990s, headed up by frontman Trevor Hurst."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Balancing Music and Nursing
xref.body: Hurst had to quit his nursing position when Econoline Crush became seriously reactivated, but he still expresses a love for the work and indicates he might return to it, acknowledging that "the music thing just can't last forever." "When a car line crush was seriously reactivated and started getting back to work, Trevor had to quit his nurse gig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Return to Education for Psychiatric Nursing
xref.body: After Econoline Crush's initial breakup and sporadic returns, Trevor Hurst, at age 45, enrolled in a psychiatric nursing program at Brandon University in 2011. This decision was driven by financial needs (having four kids), an interest in psychology, and his personal history with alcohol and addiction demons. "So in 2011, Trevor went back to school at the age of 45."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Studio Ownership and Academia
xref.body: Sylvia Massy owned her own studio for many years, which was a popular choice for bands like Sublime and Econoline Crush. Additionally, she has served as a visiting professor at Berklee College of Music and conducted workshops for the Abbey Road Institute, demonstrating her commitment to educating the next generation of audio professionals. "Sylvia owned her own studio for years, a place booked by Sublime, Econoline Crush and Dozens of Others."
